findings.statement: The ticket lists "run tests and evals", but no eval corpus, golden task or grader exists and evals are assigned to Phase 7 (STORY-008), so whether this milestone runs anything beyond the repository's own test suite is unsettled.

Whether /implement ships any mechanical protection against editing acceptance.feature, or only the stated rule, is unsettled: README Phase 6 and STORY-007's Out of Scope both assign contract immutability to a later milestone, yet the gate exempts .amigos/** so nothing refuses the edit today.

The request does not say whether this story includes actually running /implement against a real story, or whether shipping the skill is the whole deliverable — v0.4 deliberately did not close until its dogfooding run produced a number.

The milestone's exit criterion — "moves from a ready contract to verified implementation without redefining the requirement" — names no evidence: it does not say which story demonstrates it, what counts as "verified", or what artefact shows the requirement was not redefined.

The command signature is a story id alone, and the request does not say what /implement does when the invoking user adds instructions beyond the contract, which is the main path by which scope re-enters after the gate has been satisfied.

"Check for scope expansion" does not say what the change is compared against — constraints.md's Relevant Components, intent.md's Out of Scope, or the diff alone — nor whether a detected expansion stops the run or is only reported.

"Report discrepancies" does not say where the report goes; /amigos is forbidden from writing commentary into the story directory and puts its run evidence in .amigos/runs/, so whether an implement run leaves any durable record or only speaks in chat is undecided.
"Establish a baseline where useful" reads either as running the existing suite before any change or as requiring the new tests to fail first, and the two produce different observable evidence.

Nothing states what /implement does with a Then clause it cannot express as an automated test — several clauses in this repository's own contracts assert on prompt text or on a file's absence — nor whether such a clause blocks the run or is reported and skipped.

The request covers only the ready and not-ready cases; it says nothing about a story id that does not exist, or a contract the validator cannot read at all (exit code 2) as distinct from one evaluated and found not ready.

"Implement the minimum required behavior" has no stated arbiter: minimal against the acceptance scenarios and minimal against intent.md's In Scope can differ, and nothing says which governs when they do.

README section 14 tells /implement to read dor.json for "ready": true, while docs/component-design/gate.md states a committed dor.json is a record and never an authority because the gated agent can write it; the contract must settle which rule /implement follows.

Declaring contract_change on discovering a contract problem withholds readiness, after which the gate refuses the partially written code; the request does not say whether that partial work is reverted, left in place, or committed before the declaration.

Whether an implemented story is recorded anywhere is unsettled: the lifecycle has no declared state between ready and the next contract change, so nothing distinguishes a ready story that has been built from one that has not.

The request does not say whether /implement performs git operations — creating the branch that lets the gate resolve the story, staging, committing — or assumes a resolvable active story already exists in the environment.
The skill is shipped to downstream repositories whose build and test commands it cannot know; .amigos/config.json carries no test command and the request does not say how one is discovered.

Packaging beyond skills/implement/SKILL.md is unsettled: README section 19 also names a CLAUDE.md repository rule this checkout does not contain, and section 20 names a Codex mirror the roadmap defers.

README section 14's "business code" is never reconciled with the gate's "governed files", so whether /implement may write exempt paths such as docs/ while a story is not ready is open to two readings.
Whether a single /implement run must complete a whole story, and what happens when it cannot — resumption, partial delivery, a second run over the same contract — is not addressed.

tests/test_dogfooding.py enumerates this repository's story ids and excludes STORY-006, so closing this milestone changes a governed test file as a side effect, and the same happens for whichever story /implement is first used on.
